Author: Sanjay Kumar Dwivedi

 In The High Court Of Jharkhand, Ranchi
 A.B.A. No. 1735 of 2024
 ----
 Sushil Hansda .... Petitioner
 -- Versus --
 The State of Jharkhand and Another .... Opposite Parties
 ----
Coram: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Sanjay Kumar Dwivedi
---
For the Petitioner :- Mr. Rishu Ranjan, Advocate For the State :- Mr. Bishawambhar Shastri,
Advocate
----
4/10.05.2024
Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner as well as the learned counsel for the State.

2. The petitioner is apprehending his arrest in connection with Complaint Case No.2408 of 2022,
for the offence registered under sections 498A of the IPC, pending in the court of learned Sub Divisional Judicial Magistrate, Godda.

3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner is husband of the complainant and he further submits that earlier the FIR was registered in which the police has submitted the final form and nobody has been sent up for trial and on protest petition, the learned court has been pleased to take cognizance under section 498A of the IPC against the petitioner.
4. Learned State counsel opposed the prayer on the ground that the petitioner is the husband of the complainant.

5. Considering that police in investigation has exonerated the petitioner and on protest petition, the learned court has been pleased to take cognizance against the petitioner and the case is arising out of section 498A of the IPC, and in the attending facts and circumstances, I am inclined to provide privilege of anticipatory bail to the petitioner.

sentences.text: Accordingly, the petitioner, above named, is hereby directed to surrender before the learned court within three weeks from today, and in the event of his surrender/arrest, the petitioner, above named, shall be released on bail, on furnishing bail bond of Rs.25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand), with two sureties of the like amount each, to the satisfaction of learned Sub Divisional Judicial Magistrate, Godda, in connection with Complaint Case No.2408 of 2022, subject to the conditions as laid down under section 438(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

( Sanjay Kumar Dwivedi, J.) SI/
